newsitem.title: UK: EU, Mexican sugar orders feature on freight market.
newsitem.headline: EU, Mexican sugar orders feature on freight market.

text.p: The sugar freight market perked up in midweek as demand was noted for both European and Mexican sugars to be shipped into Africa, shipbrokers said on Wednesday.
E D & F Man was said to have fixed a bagged parcel of 9/11,000 tonnes from Eemshaven to Lagos for mid-March.

Man also featured on the list of new inquiries, quoting for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Veracruz or Coatzacoalcos to Algeria for prompt dates and 6,000 tonnes from Durban to Dar es Salaam for early March.
Czarnikow was open for 3,000 tonnes in bags from Denmark to Nigeria for prompt dates, shipbrokers said.
CSR was rumoured to be in the market with a cargo of 26,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland but more details were not immediately available, they said.

Cargill fixed two of its previous orders for Thai bulk sugar, covering 18,000 tonnes to south Korea/Japan for early March and a 8,000-tonne parcel to Japan only for 1/15 March. Details of rates have yet to emerge.
In other news, Iraq has postponed its tender to buy sugar under the U.N. oil-for-food deal until February 28 but the amount required remains unclear.

The original tender called for 120,000 tonnes of sugar but some traders said Iraq might only be in the marlet to take two cargoes of 12,500 tonnes. Shipment dates are unlikely to become clear until the sales are granted U.N. approval.
Syria tenders on Wednesday to buy 13,000 tonnes of white sugar and 13,000 tonnes of raw for April shipment.
